question: Does the S11 corpus-coverage abstention rule transfer, unchanged, to the frozen external KnowledgeDrift sample?
answer: NO. No threshold in the declared grid meets the pre-registered bar.
prereg_bar: correct abstentions materially above the 0/40 floor while losing <= 8 of 80 useful retrievals

headline.at_threshold_0.5: 0/40 correct abstentions, 10/80 useful retrievals lost - strictly worse than not applying the rule

mechanism: KnowledgeDrift builds unanswerable questions by recombining vocabulary the corpus already contains. 'ashen estuary ingest job retry budget' scores supported_fraction 6/6: every term occurs in some record, no record holds the combination. A per-term coverage test cannot see a novel combination of covered terms. The only queries it does reject are ones whose ordinary words ('decide','about') happen to be absent.
what_this_says_about_the_prior_result: S11-ABSTAIN3's 5/5 was measured on cases this project wrote, whose irrelevant queries were irrelevant IN VOCABULARY. The external benchmark's distractors are not. The prior result stands as reported for its own cases and does not generalise.
scope: 120 frozen probes (40 Abstention, 40 Retrieval, 40 Rationale) across two sha-pinned worlds. No parameter tuned. No threshold selected after results. Sample not re-drawn; 0 unresolved, 0 degenerate.
limits: Abstention correctness is 'declined or not', not 'declined for the right reason'.
40 probes per family across two seeds; no confidence interval claimed.
The benchmark author has a competing system in its own published ranking.
This measures one rule on one external sample. It says nothing about whether memory improves real work.

corrections.now: 'answerable probes rejected'. The runner never ran BM25 and never joined against successful baseline retrievals, so it does NOT establish that those probes would have been answered. The conservative count stands under the accurate name; the destroyed-answers claim is withdrawn.

corrections.kind: rule implementation deviated from the frozen rule
corrections.was: content terms as a LIST, counting repetitions
corrections.now: sorted(set(query)) - stopwords, matching S11 coverage(). REPAIR ATTEMPT 1 of 2. Result: IDENTICAL at all five thresholds. attempt 1 preserved at results-attempt1-repeated-tokens.json.

corrections.was: attempt 2 was computed in an ad-hoc inline script; run_transfer.py still counted token OCCURRENCES and the verdict pinned that old runner's hash. A result existed with no code on disk that produced it.
corrections.now: run_transfer.py repaired to sorted(set(tok(query))) - STOP, re-run from the file, results.json regenerated by it. Runner and results hashes both pinned above. Grid identical at all five thresholds, third time.
this is ATTEMPT 2 = repair 1 of 1, under the one-initial-plus-one-repair budget. The budget is now spent.

open_fidelity_issues: CORPUS SEMANTICS: this run pools every inscribe record across the stream, including records later retired, and does not ingest supersede replacements. S10-KD-CROSS's baseline replays updates and removals and queries the live store at each recall. Pooling also lets later inscriptions affect earlier queries. The direction of the mismatch is NOT established as one-directional. Unresolved; it is the strongest remaining objection to the result.

REGISTRATION ORDER NOT DEMONSTRATED: registration, runner and results entered git together in 99d8f6f. A hash proves content identity, not chronology. This row does not exercise the earlier-commit check the loop proposal relies on.

'MATERIALLY ABOVE' the 0/40 floor was never given a number. It does not rescue this grid (every threshold with abstentions already breaches the loss limit) but would make a borderline positive ambiguous.
status: negative result stands; runner now bound to results; repair budget SPENT; three fidelity issues open; verified_by still null
